title: Universal lifting from glued thickening charts
statement: Let h : Z → X be a morphism of schemes and C an open cover of Z indexed in the schemes universe. Suppose explicit schemes Z′_k and maps i_k : C_k → Z′_k, h′_k : Z′_k → X are supplied and each is a universal first order thickening over X for C.f_k ≫ h [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]. Then there exist W, j : Z → W and p : W → X such that j with p is a universal first order thickening of h. No formal unramifiedness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), proof, fourth and fifth paragraphs; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04F3

proof.text: Apply the glued-atlas construction to obtain W, j, p and an open cover D of W, with j first order, j ≫ p = h, and universality on each chart. It remains to prove the universal property for arbitrary tests.

For a test t : T → T′, b : T′ → X and a : T → Z whose composite a ≫ j lands in one chart of D, factor a ≫ j uniquely through that open immersion and lift a into the pullback source chart. Local universality gives a lift into the chart and hence into W. Any competing lift into W also lands in the chart, since t is surjective on points; cancellation of the chart inclusion and local uniqueness identify it with the constructed lift.

For any test thickening t, the first clause of universalFirstOrderThickening_open_pieces gives uniqueness of an open with specified inverse image. The complement of the closed image of t and the empty open have the same empty inverse image; uniqueness makes that complement empty. Thus t is surjective, and its closed embedding is a homeomorphism. Transfer the inverse-image cover of T induced by a ≫ j and D to T′. Restricted tests are first order by the same existing theorem. The single-chart uniqueness argument then proves equality locally, hence globally.

On this transferred test cover, the single-chart lifting argument supplies local solutions. On pairwise overlaps pull back t along the open intersection; the closed immersion and square-zero condition persist, the latter by restriction of kernel ideals. Global uniqueness from the previous step identifies the two restricted solutions. Glue the local morphisms into W; both triangle identities follow from equality after restriction to the respective covers of T′ and T. The uniqueness already proved gives the unique lift. Together with the glued-atlas clauses this is the claimed universal thickening.

lean.statement:
theorem universalFirstOrderThickening_glue
    {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ X) (C : Z.OpenCover.{u})
    (Z' : C.I₀ → Scheme.{u}) (i : ∀ k, C.X k ⟶ Z' k)
    (h' : ∀ k, Z' k ⟶ X)
    (H : ∀ k, IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening (C.f k ≫ h) (i k) (h' k)) :
    ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (j : Z ⟶ W) (p : W ⟶ X),
      IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening h j p
